subject.title: fix(memory): use FTS-only when optional embeddings are unavailable

question: Should memory_search return read-only, potentially stale FTS results from an existing semantic index when an optional embedding provider disappears and synchronization is intentionally refused?
rationale: The branch correctly preserves the vector index, but choosing availability over freshness changes what successful memory search means for existing users; code inspection and tests cannot determine the intended user contract.

options.title: Accept read-only FTS fallback
options.body: Land the fallback as an intentional degraded mode and make the stale/read-only status discoverable to users.

options.title: Keep paused semantics
options.body: Preserve the current safety posture by withholding searches until embeddings are available again or the user explicitly rebuilds the index.

options.title: Add an explicit opt-in policy
options.body: Keep the existing default and expose stale FTS search only through an approved, documented configuration or recovery choice.

recommendation.title: Accept read-only FTS fallback
recommendation.body: Land the fallback as an intentional degraded mode and make the stale/read-only status discoverable to users.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a repository-level memory behavior and upgrade-contract decision rather than a contributor repair task.
